bull_bear.body:
- Long-standing business relationships with reputed customers across multiple sectors (stated in MD&A Company Overview)
- Debt-free balance sheet — the Company remained debt free during the year with negligible external borrowings and entire debt repaid, with capex funded substantially through internal accruals and operating cash flows
- Technology-enabled operational control stack — GPS-enabled fleet monitoring, CCTV-based operational monitoring, system-driven warehouse operations, digital process controls and inventory discipline mechanisms
- Two-division model where a growing Supply Chain Solutions business offsets a declining Freight Division, giving revenue stability at the total-company level
- Strong liquidity/working-capital position — current ratio of 7.90 as at 31.03.2026
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Fuel and consumable cost volatility with a pass-through lag — Management states the Company is exposed to fluctuations in prices of operational inputs including fuel, tyres, lubricants and other transportation-related consumables, which 'may impact operating margins until corresponding revisions are implemented' — i.e. price increases hit margins before customer rate revisions catch up. Fuel price volatility is also named as an industry-level challenge and in the cautionary statement.
- Manpower and driver availability, and rising manpower / compliance costs — Driver availability and rising manpower and compliance costs are named among the industry's structural challenges, and manpower availability is listed among the Company's own risks. For a road-transport and warehouse-operations business where labour is the second cost pillar after fuel, scarcity translates directly into cost and into service failures.
- Customer demand fluctuations and dependence on a customer base concentrated in a few sectors — Customer demand fluctuations are explicitly listed among the Company's risks, and demand is described as coming from FMCG, pharmaceuticals, consumer products, industrial goods and organized retail. The Company's positioning rests on 'long-standing business relationships with reputed customers', which is also a dependency — the AR gives no diversification metrics.
- Competitive pricing pressure in a formalising logistics market — Competitive pricing pressures are named as a risk, and the industry narrative points to rising customer expectations on service quality and turnaround timelines — a combination that raises the service bar while capping realisations. Freight Division revenue fell to ₹28.46 Crores in FY2025-26 from ₹31.34 Crores, with the Company describing its response as 'operational optimization and disciplined cost management' rather than growth.
- Infrastructure constraints and operational disruptions, including weather — Infrastructure constraints and operational disruptions are listed among the Company's risks; the industry section additionally names weather-related operational disruptions. These directly affect turnaround times and fleet utilisation — the very metrics the Freight Division is managed on.
- Safety risk across transportation and warehousing operations — Safety risks are explicitly listed among the Company's risks. The response described is procedural — PPE compliance, fleet safety monitoring, CCTV-enabled operational monitoring, fire and electrical safety, equipment safety practices and driver awareness initiatives — which signals the exposure is live rather than eliminated.
- Regulatory change and compliance burden — Regulatory changes are named among the Company's risks and government regulations appear in the cautionary statement as a factor that could cause actual results to differ materially. Rising compliance costs are separately flagged as an industry-level challenge.
- Earnings exposure to fair-value movements on mutual fund investments — Management states that profitability during the year was impacted by fair valuation adjustments relating to mutual fund investments accounted for under applicable Indian Accounting Standards — so reported profit carries a mark-to-market component from treasury holdings that is unrelated to the logistics operations.

outlook.body:
- Pivot the mix towards warehousing and integrated supply chain solutions — the Company states it intends to continue focusing on warehousing and supply chain solutions and to strengthen its presence in integrated logistics, warehousing and allied supply chain services

- Defend the Freight Division through fleet utilization, route optimization, turnaround management, preventive maintenance and disciplined cost management rather than volume growth
- Maintain financial prudence — stay debt free, fund capex from internal accruals and operating cash flows, and plough back profits instead of paying a dividend so as to strengthen the reserve position for future warehousing/supply-chain growth

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report describes no named expansion project, no commissioning or ramp timeline and no capacity addition. Expansion, such as it is, is described only as organic scaling of the warehousing footprint: the Company says it continued operations at organized warehousing facilities including system-driven operations catering to institutional customers, and attributes the increase in warehouse-related operational expenses during the year to 'scaling up of warehousing and supply chain activities'. On the asset side, the only investment language is that the Company remained debt free and that capital expenditure incurred during the year, including additions to operational vehicle assets, was substantially funded through internal accruals and operating cash flows, with continued investment in operational assets. Forward intent is limited to continuing to focus on warehousing and supply chain solutions and infrastructure strengthening, and to evaluating evolving operational technologies including material handling solutions, warehouse process improvements and alternate mobility solutions wherever operationally feasible — none of which is attached to a site, a quantum or a date.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Increasing formalization of logistics and warehousing operations, growth in organized distribution networks and increasing focus on integrated supply chain solutions are described as providing long-term growth opportunities
- The Indian logistics and supply chain sector is said to be undergoing gradual structural transformation driven by organized distribution growth, infrastructure development, increasing outsourcing of logistics functions and technology adoption
- Demand for integrated logistics solutions — transportation, warehousing and inventory management — continued across FMCG, pharmaceuticals, consumer products, industrial goods and organized retail
- The warehousing and supply chain segment is seeing increasing customer focus on inventory visibility, technology-enabled monitoring, process standardization and system-driven warehouse operations — the capabilities the Company is investing in
- Headwinds named: fuel price volatility, rising manpower and compliance costs, infrastructure constraints, driver availability, weather-related disruptions and rising customer expectations on service quality and turnaround times
- Warehouse-related operational expenses rose during the year, which management attributes to scaling up of warehousing and supply chain activities
- Finance costs reduced on lower borrowing levels; profitability during the year was impacted by fair valuation adjustments on mutual fund investments

risks.body:
- Fuel and consumable cost volatility with a pass-through lag — Management states the Company is exposed to fluctuations in prices of operational inputs including fuel, tyres, lubricants and other transportation-related consumables, which 'may impact operating margins until corresponding revisions are implemented' — i.e. price increases hit margins before customer rate revisions catch up. Fuel price volatility is also named as an industry-level challenge and in the cautionary statement.
- Manpower and driver availability, and rising manpower / compliance costs — Driver availability and rising manpower and compliance costs are named among the industry's structural challenges, and manpower availability is listed among the Company's own risks. For a road-transport and warehouse-operations business where labour is the second cost pillar after fuel, scarcity translates directly into cost and into service failures.
- Customer demand fluctuations and dependence on a customer base concentrated in a few sectors — Customer demand fluctuations are explicitly listed among the Company's risks, and demand is described as coming from FMCG, pharmaceuticals, consumer products, industrial goods and organized retail. The Company's positioning rests on 'long-standing business relationships with reputed customers', which is also a dependency — the AR gives no diversification metrics.
- Competitive pricing pressure in a formalising logistics market — Competitive pricing pressures are named as a risk, and the industry narrative points to rising customer expectations on service quality and turnaround timelines — a combination that raises the service bar while capping realisations. Freight Division revenue fell to ₹28.46 Crores in FY2025-26 from ₹31.34 Crores, with the Company describing its response as 'operational optimization and disciplined cost management' rather than growth.
- Infrastructure constraints and operational disruptions, including weather — Infrastructure constraints and operational disruptions are listed among the Company's risks; the industry section additionally names weather-related operational disruptions. These directly affect turnaround times and fleet utilisation — the very metrics the Freight Division is managed on.
- Safety risk across transportation and warehousing operations — Safety risks are explicitly listed among the Company's risks. The response described is procedural — PPE compliance, fleet safety monitoring, CCTV-enabled operational monitoring, fire and electrical safety, equipment safety practices and driver awareness initiatives — which signals the exposure is live rather than eliminated.
- Regulatory change and compliance burden — Regulatory changes are named among the Company's risks and government regulations appear in the cautionary statement as a factor that could cause actual results to differ materially. Rising compliance costs are separately flagged as an industry-level challenge.
- Earnings exposure to fair-value movements on mutual fund investments — Management states that profitability during the year was impacted by fair valuation adjustments relating to mutual fund investments accounted for under applicable Indian Accounting Standards — so reported profit carries a mark-to-market component from treasury holdings that is unrelated to the logistics operations.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Pivot the mix towards warehousing and integrated supply chain solutions — the Company states it intends to continue focusing on warehousing and supply chain solutions and to strengthen its presence in integrated logistics, warehousing and allied supply chain services
- Run process-driven, technology-enabled operations: GPS-enabled fleet monitoring, CCTV-based operational monitoring, system-driven warehouse operations, digital process controls and inventory discipline mechanisms
- Defend the Freight Division through fleet utilization, route optimization, turnaround management, preventive …

hero.oneLiner: Coastal Roadways Limited is a BSE-listed, debt-free logistics company running freight transportation alongside a growing warehousing and integrated supply-chain solutions business, with FY2025-26 revenue from operations of ₹41.37 Crores.
